claims.head: Iron sharpens iron
claims.body: The Hurricanes are near the top of the league for the power play, but the Blues are near the top at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Hurricanes’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
claims.call: The Hurricanes’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.6 expected goals per 60 against the Blues.
claims.nums: Carolina 7th for the power play (8.2 expected goals per 60) · St. Louis 8th for the penalty kill

chips.tip: Carolina: 8.2 expected goals per 60 on the power play, 7th of 32. Playing style, this season blended with last, 12 and 10 games this season.
St. Louis: 7.2 expected goals allowed per 60 shorthanded, 8th of 32. Playing style, this season blended with last, 12 and 10 games this season.

claims.head: Power vs. Power
claims.call: The Blues’ L1 (Holloway, Thomas and Snuggerud) spends at least 44% of its 5-on-5 time against the Hurricanes’ first line, against about 31% with no line matching.
claims.body: At home, the Blues keep sending Thomas’s line (Holloway, Thomas and Snuggerud) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jim Montgomery has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Hurricanes’ first line is Carrier, Aho and Svechnikov.
claims.nums: At home: 57% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 31% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Jim Montgomery likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Hurricanes’ first line.
claims.cite: Matchups · St. Louis home games this season · 4 games, 56 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

chips.tip: St. Louis’s L1 (Holloway, Thomas and Snuggerud) at home: 57% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ first lines. Matchups, St. Louis home games this season, 4 games, 56 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 31% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

stakes: The Hurricanes go in first in the NHL with 18 points, the Blues tied for fifth in the Central with 11 points.

STL.head: The Blues start a half-step behind
STL.body: Even though St. Louis has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Blues’ best way to tip it is getting good looks.

CAR.head: The Hurricanes have a slight edge
CAR.body: Even though St. Louis has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. Still, it’s close: the Blues can make it interesting if they get good looks.

story.head: Iron sharpens iron
paras: The Blues have won two in a row, the last a 6-2 rout of Vegas. The Hurricanes are 8-2-2.

It’s strength against strength: the Hurricanes are near the top of the league for the power play, but the Blues are near the top at the penalty kill. At home, Jim Montgomery likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Canes’ first line.

lean.STL: Even though St. Louis has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Blues’ best way to tip it is getting good looks.
lean.CAR: Even though St. Louis has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. Still, it’s close: the Blues can make it interesting if they get good looks.
